name: Nourish & Co. Kitchen Service Uniform Set
description:
The standard uniform for kitchen workers at Nourish & Co. contracted canteens — the corporate cafeteria chains that feed the working population of GLMZ's Tier 2 and 3 commercial zones. The set includes a double-breasted chef coat in heat-resistant spun polyaramid, a bib apron with a wipe-clean surface coating, and adjustable trouser pulls. The coat is rated for sustained heat up to 260°C and resists oil, acid, and most cleaning chemical splashes. Color is white with Nourish & Co.'s green-stripe trim. The apron has an embedded RFID tag that logs when it's collected and returned from the facility's laundry system — a measure ostensibly for inventory control.

The uniform is produced in configurations that address the full range of kitchen workers in 2200: the coat collar includes a snap-out panel for workers with neck-mounted chrome or BCI hardware, and alternative headgear options include structured caps with horn-clearance inserts and elasticized wraps that conform to ear modifications or unusual head shapes. The standard hairnet alternative for workers with bioluminescent or modified skin is a full-coverage food-safe skull cap. The uniform is the property of the facility, not the worker, and must be returned at end of employment — a fact enforced by the RFID logging system.
cultural_context: Kitchen work in M88 is grueling, essential, and chronically undervalued. The Nourish & Co. uniform marks you as part of the invisible infrastructure that feeds the city. Workers develop strong bonds with their kitchen crews — the uniform is shared, the work is shared, and the complaints about the RFID tracking are universal.
story_hooks: The RFID logging system in a Nourish & Co. canteen has been cross-referencing uniform collection times with worker political association data — someone is using the laundry system as a surveillance tool.
A kitchen worker discovers that her facility's food supply chain runs through a Crucible subsidiary that's been substituting synthetic protein sources without disclosure.
A Tier 4 corporate dining facility that uses Nourish & Co. contract staff has a contamination incident — and the kitchen workers are being pressured to sign NDAs before anyone investigates.

physical_description.visual_profile: Crisp, utilitarian silhouette with institutional precision. White chef coat dominates, accented by kelly green trim at collar, cuffs, and button placket. Bib apron extends from chest to mid-thigh, creating a clean rectangular plane. Overall impression: sterile efficiency with subtle hints of wear on a well-maintained work garment.
physical_description.fit: Double-breasted coat sits structured but not constrictive—designed for movement in tight kitchen spaces. Sleeves taper at wrist with ribbed cuffs. Apron has reinforced straps over shoulders, slightly loose through the torso to accommodate layering and repeated bending. Trousers pull-on style with adjustable waist for quick changes between shifts.
physical_description.primary_material: Heat-resistant spun polyaramid (coat), wipe-clean polymer-coated cotton-weave (apron), stretch-blend twill (trousers)
physical_description.texture: Coat fabric has a tight, almost crisp weave with slight sheen from polyaramid treatment. Apron surface is slick and moisture-repellent, designed to shed liquids instantly. Trousers have subtle texture—broken-in softness from multiple washes but maintained structure.
physical_description.color_scheme: Stark white as primary with kelly green accent stripes. Nourish & Co. logo (small, green-on-white) appears on left chest and apron bib. Minor off-white discoloration and faint staining typical on deployed uniforms—bleach spots, heat-fade marks, set-in grease shadows.
physical_description.closures: Double-breasted magnetic snaps down coat front (faster than buttons for quick changes). Apron secured with canvas ties at waist and neck. Trousers use friction-fit elastic waistband with drawstring.
distinctive_features: Snap-out neck collar panel for workers with chrome hardware or subcutaneous BCI ports
Reinforced cuff panels rated for 260°C sustained heat
Small RFID patch embedded in apron seam (inventory tracking/monitoring)
Alternative cap options: structured with horn-clearance inserts or elasticized skull-cap style for modified workers
Double-reinforced apron bib with secondary catch pocket for small utensils
Acid and oil-resistant treatment visible as slight water-beading on surface
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 functional. Clean, durable, unremarkable. Signals essential work rather than prestige. Corporate-standardized rather than individual choice.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this marks you as part of GLMZ's invisible kitchen infrastructure—the people who feed the city. Among kitchen crews, it signals belonging to a tight-knit, overworked collective. To outsiders, it's nearly invisible—the uniform of people whose labor is essential but socially unnoticed. The RFID tag is a point of collective grievance and dark humor among wearers.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but visibly used. White retains brightness through facility laundering but shows faint discoloration patterns—grease shadows, bleach spots, heat-fade. Apron may have small creases or impressions from repeated folding. Magnetic snaps occasionally loose or replaced. Overall impression: clean, functional, worn with the weight of repetition.

image_prompt: A Tier 3 kitchen worker in full Nourish & Co. uniform—white heat-resistant chef coat with kelly green trim, matching apron, adjustable trousers—standing in a dimly lit industrial canteen kitchen. Overhead fluorescent bars cast cool shadows across stainless steel counters and walk-in freezer doors visible in background. Worker's expression is tired but composed. Close detail shot of apron showing wipe-clean polymer coating catching light, small RFID tag visible in seam. Moody, desaturated color palette with pops of that institutional green. Shot from waist up, professional but intimate. Documentary-style neo-noir foodservice authenticity. --ar 2:3 --v 6
